verdict: At the top 20% of road length, the model (road features only, no death history) captured 78% of later deaths versus 58% for the best past-deaths baseline (past deaths on the same road): +24 points, 95% interval +16 to +33. At the top 10% it was 54% versus 52%: +2 points, interval −6 to +12 (a tie). The model combined with past deaths on the same road did best at the top 10%: 59%, +7 points, interval +2 to +13. The test set is small (127 deaths), so treat these as estimates.
features: distance to a bus stop (less risk)
second_region: Cleveland, OH: trained on 2019–2021, tested on 2022–2023 (29 deaths). Road features only captured 66% of later deaths in the top 20% of road length vs 52% for the best past-deaths baseline (+21 points, 95% interval +3 to +38); at the top 10%: 55% vs 45% (+10, interval −7 to +28).
